paraphrase: Buddhaghosa explains the six names: Pūraṇa, a slave, 'completed' a hundred slaves; Makkhali, told 'don't stumble' (mā khali) while carrying an oil-pot, ran off naked; Ajita wore a blanket of human hair; he glosses Makkhali's lists, including the 'eight stages of a person' as stages of life from the dull newborn to the one who has gone forth and beyond.
notes: Reported by an opponent: Buddhaghosa (Theravāda commentary). From memory; not verified locally.

paraphrase: The introduction tells how the canon was recited at the First Council and entrusted to reciter lineages (bhāṇaka), and records that the Dīgha-reciters and Majjhima-reciters classified the Khuddaka books differently.
